issues.legal_issue: A tribunal cannot refuse to give effect to a final High Court order in the same matter by relying on a later contrary judgment.
material_facts: The High Court had quashed the land-vesting proceedings in the appellants’ case, and the State did not challenge that order, so it remained in force.
The appellants later asked the tribunal to correct the revenue records in accordance with the High Court order.
The tribunal rejected the application by relying on a later, contrary single-judge decision, and the High Court affirmed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal had no jurisdiction to differ from the earlier High Court order, and the High Court and tribunal orders were set aside. The tribunal was directed to follow the earlier order.
issues.legal_principle: A court or tribunal must give effect to an operative High Court order in the same matter unless it has been set aside by a larger bench or a superior court. A later contrary decision, including a later single-judge decision, does not by itself authorize the tribunal to disregard that order. The Court described this as a settled principle; the appellants had referred to the Explanation to Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and to Nand Kishore Ahirwar v. Haridas Parsedia and Shanti Devi v. State of Haryana, but the judgment does not identify those authorities as the basis for its holding.

predicates.tribunal_application_following_high_cour: A person applies to a tribunal for action consistent with an earlier High Court order in that matter.
predicates.prior_order_remained_unset: The earlier High Court order has not been set aside by a larger bench or a superior court.
predicates.tribunal_rejected_application_based_on_l: The tribunal rejects the application because it relies on a later decision that takes a contrary view.

issues.definition: When a tribunal receives an application following an unset High Court order and rejects it on the basis of a later contrary decision, it must give effect to the earlier High Court order.
